newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel boosts tax relief for approved enterprises.
newsitem.headline: Israel boosts tax relief for approved enterprises.

text.p: Israel's parliamentary finance committee approved a bill that would ease tax requirements for factories in highest priority development areas, the Trade and Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
"The parliament finance committee approved last Friday the proposed bill presented by the minister of trade and industry and the finance minister," a ministry statement said.

It said the measure would exempt approved enterprises in development zone A areas from paying corporate income tax for two years and let them pay a reduced rate of 25 percent for the following five years.
Under current law, approved enterprises in A zones pay corporate tax at the reduced 25 percent rate for the first seven years of operation. The regular rate is 36 percent.
The law now goes to parliamentary vote.
The ministry said the measure was part of a programme of changes and improvements made to compensate for a reduction in grants provided to approved enterprises.
